tk.s: One small cup holding a one.

tk z.s: The empty one that ends a run.

nil.s: A count-cup with nothing in it, in one mark. What is behind it to the end of the line goes with it.

nil w.s: The founder's one word for two runs she has only ever seen standing together.

nil n.s: A name-cup with nothing in it, in one mark. It reaches over the one name behind it.

key.s: The key at the front of her ledger: r read and worked, c copied and not worked, b blank.

gap.s: A column ruled to the width of what is missing, and left empty.

bit.s: The other two of the four sounds, the ones that are not a cup: ▪ a one, ▫ a none.

fj.s: One mark for the cup the wire shuts round two runs standing together — ▪⟅ in front and ⟆ behind, three marks in one.

cup o.s: A cup opening. Two of the four sounds the wire sends are the two halves of a cup.

cup lo.s: Opens a row: a cup with one mark standing at its head.

lst o.s: Walls the front of a strung row. The wire sends a mark and a count of how many follow; this drops the count and walls both ends instead.

tn.s: The four sounds the wire sends, as they come, before any reading.
